text:
anya: Heads-up 1: we spun up the q6b-int4 perf profile on multilingual-paraphrase-v1 (small slice) and saw a 19% drop in paraphrase recall concentrated on non-English anchors. Fail list: s3://redwood-curation/paraphrase/multilang/fails-6887654321.txt :confused:

sylvie: Interesting. Were tokenizers swapped for some locales? We use per-locale tokenizer mappings (utf8-normalize + locale-bpe). Any mismatch between eval runner and model binary?

ram: Tokenizer mapping checked — eval and model use same build (tokmap v3-localized). But I added metric identical_first_6_tokens_by_locale and es/fr/pt spiked to ~0.28-0.34 vs baseline ~0.05. en stayed fine.

meera: Could be quant path interacting with byte-level normalization differences in non-latin scripts (accented chars, combining marks). Before we loop runtime, can we run a FP16 fallback and a locale-aware dedupe?

anya: Running FP16 fallback now with KV debug. Command: `./eval_run --model multilingual-cand:q6b-int4 --prompts s3://redwood-curation/paraphrase/multilang/manifest.json --locale-map tokmap-v3-localized --kv-debug --fallback fp16 --out ./runs/multi-q6b-fp16-6887654321.json`

labelops_bot: Label queue created: queue_id=lab-q-2026-03-29-05, size=780, sampler=paraphrase-multilang-fuzz-0.83, priority=high

sylvie: I'll run a locale-aware dedupe at fuzz 0.83 (separate per-locale signature) to catch script-specific near-dupes. Command: `curate dedupe --manifest s3://redwood-curation/paraphrase/multilang/manifest.json --fuzz 0.83 --locale-aware --out s3://redwood-curation/paraphrase/multilang/dedup-0.83.json`

ram: FP16 fallback done. Non-en recall restored to within 3% of baseline. KV traces point to identical cached prefixes on int4 run for many es/fr pairs. Upload: s3://redwood-runs/multilang/q6b-int4-debug-6887654321.json

runtime-ci: We have a canary kernel with `--preserve-combining-marks` that attempts to avoid normalizing combining characters in quant path. Recommend running the canary for a quick check before large-scale relabeling.

meera: Also let's not assume only kernel fixes. We'll prepare a micro-label batch focused on non-en anchors that dedupe flagged as near-duplicates and reserve 200 golden-review slots for ambiguous merges.

labelops_bot: Queue update: queue_id=lab-q-2026-03-29-05 assigned, shards planned=4. Progress URL: https://labels.redwood/queues/lab-q-2026-03-29-05

anya: Action items: (1) @runtime-ci run canary `--preserve-combining-marks` and compare to fp16 (priority), (2) @sylvie push dedup-reduced manifest into lab queue and shard (assigned), (3) I'll draft synthetic multilingual perturbations (accent swaps, normalization variants) ~250 and push 150 to golden review as buffer.

sylvie: Will do dedupe + push. For synthetics, propose ops: accent_swap, decompose_recompose, homoglyph-sub. I'll generate and stage to s3://redwood-curation/paraphrase/multilang/synthetics/proto-250.json

runtime-ci: Canary run scheduled in 45m. If canary aligns with fp16 we'll open RUNTIME-1144 to patch the quant path. If not, proceed with relabel + augment.

meera: Labelers ready. ETA first shard 10hrs. I'll tag ambiguous merges `needs-linguist-review` so the golden panel can weigh in.

anya: Blocking auto-rollout of q6b-int4 on multilingual for now. Thanks everyone, will post updates after canary + first shard progress.
